summary.headline: CMS Info Systems Q2 FY27: services revenue hit a record Rs 644 crore (+16.2% YoY); Tech & Payments reached 20% of services revenue, two quarters early.
summary.overview: Services revenue was a record Rs 644 crore, up 16.2% YoY and 3% QoQ, with EBITDA of Rs 173 crore (26.7% margin) up 24.8% YoY. Management attributed the year's pressure to a currency supply disruption from February to August, a steep rise in statutory minimum wages in several states and an 8% rise in fuel costs, which hit transaction-linked ATM revenue. H1 operating cash flow turned positive at Rs 177 crore versus an outflow of Rs 117 crore a year earlier, and FY27 guidance was revised. Analyst questions focused on receivables, capex accounting, depreciation, and the non-banking (Hawkeye) competitive position, where answers were partly unclear.

segments.name: Cash management
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 404 crore (+2% YoY) with EBIT Rs 77 crore at 19.1% margin. Management says the ATM-linked volume recovery is still incomplete; average dispense per ATM per day is up 8% but about 10% below last year.

segments.name: Managed services (incl. cards)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 321 crore (+19% YoY) with EBIT Rs 34 crore at 10.6% margin. Lower transaction-linked ATM revenue and higher depreciation from the FY26 capex cycle and FSS acquisition weighed on margin.

segments.name: Technology and payments
segments.commentary: Now 20% of services revenue in Q2 (about Rs 500 crore annualised, more than 4x FY22), versus 7% in FY22 and ahead of the 20% by Q4 target. Recent wins include a second PSU bank branch RMS mandate (650 branches) and a third Algo MBS bank with rollout across 12,000 machines.

segments.name: Product sales (recyclers)
segments.commentary: Revenue is low in H1; two recycler orders from PSU banks won in Q1 are due for delivery in H2, so product revenue should step up in H2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 services revenue guidance revised to Rs 2,650-2,750 crore.
FY27 total revenue guidance of Rs 2,750-2,800 crore (figure partly garbled in transcript; likely Rs 2,750-2,850 crore).
FY27 capex guidance of Rs 100-125 crore, versus about Rs 350 crore in FY26.
Depreciation expected to peak in FY27; management indicated roughly Rs 300 crore for FY28, about 5% above or below the Rs 290 crore run-rate implied by H1.
Management expects deposition (depreciation) as a share of revenue to fall from FY28 and EBITDA growth to flow more to earnings.
Management aims for good QoQ growth in Q3 and Q4 to build an exit run-rate into FY28; new business is all fixed-fee contracts.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 net capex was Rs 50 crore against Rs 351 crore last year; cash-flow investing outflow of about Rs 149 crore included about Rs 50 crore for Securance-related assets and about Rs 54 crore moved from CWIP to capex.
ATM capex in H1 was Rs 10.6 crore, down 63% YoY, limited to already-committed deployments.
Offsite ATMs in India fell from about 88,000 to 70,000 over two years; total ATM base steady at about 2.1 lakh; onsite ATMs growing about 4% a year.
Two recycler orders from PSU banks (won in Q1) to be delivered in H2 FY27.
Algo MBS implementation at a new bank goes live in H2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Currency in circulation at a record about Rs 43.5 lakh crore, up 13.5% YoY, the fastest growth in five years.
Currency supply disruption ran from February to August 2026; currency fulfilment was about 70% at the August call and has since recovered further.
H1 order wins were about Rs 700 crore; market share held at 60% in ATM cash management and 38% in retail cash solutions.

Statutory minimum wages rose 6% to as much as 60% in key states and fuel costs rose 8%; management says many contracts were priced years ago and a revision is being negotiated via the IBA Working Committee.
Management said it declined a Rs 700 crore transaction-priced contract in FY26 and has stayed out of most transaction-price tenders since FY25; all new business is on fixed-fee contracts.
Management said the ATM and retail solutions combined grew about 10% Q2 on Q2; retail volumes were up about 3.7-4%.
Receivable days (DSO) improved by about 18-20 days YoY in H1, per management, though absolute receivables rose.
Management said public sector bank collections take about 30-60 days longer than private-sector ones.

qa_highlights.question: Currency in circulation grew about 17% since March 2025 while cash management revenue was flat; what is the non-ATM retail and currency-in-transit volume growth over the same period?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give the exact figure. It said ATM and retail solutions together grew about 10% on a Q2-to-Q2 basis, and retail volumes were up about 3.7-4%. Contracting for volume was held back by pricing negotiations, which management expects to resolve in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Where does CMS win and lose in non-banking Hawkeye surveillance against competitors, and why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its edge is OEM-agnostic plug-and-play software, a national distribution network, and a track record in banking. It said it loses on price and on technology robustness, and that competitors include end-to-end players and system integrators. Target sectors are those with thousands of distributed sites, such as retail, NBFC branches and EV.

qa_highlights.question: Why do operating cash flow and receivables look inconsistent: receivables absorbed about Rs 100 crore and capex was about Rs 150 crore against guidance of Rs 100-125 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about Rs 50 crore of the cash outflow was for Securance and about Rs 54 crore was a transfer from CWIP, so the Rs 149 crore is not all capex. He said H1 collections were focused on and DSO improved 18-20 days, with collections typically higher in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why are bad debt write-offs and ATM cash shortage provisions added back to operating cash flow when they recur every year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said provisions are ECL-based, around 4% of cash handled, and reconciliations with customers take time. It did not fully reconcile the recurring write-offs and said it would take the question offline with the IR team.

qa_highlights.question: What is the depreciation run-rate and what does FY28 look like?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 depreciation was about Rs 146 crore, roughly Rs 290 crore annualised. Management said FY27 is the peak, with FY28 possibly around Rs 300 crore, plus or minus 5%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an acquisition pipeline or a plan for the cash beyond 12-18 months of needs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it had evaluated over 15 acquisitions and completed two (Securance and FSS CashTech), and it is looking at payments-infrastructure companies in India. Surplus cash is to go to dividends and, where it makes sense, buybacks; the decision would be reviewed at fiscal year end.

risks_watch: Receivables and cash conversion: DSO improved, but absolute receivables rose and the reconciliation of the Rs 151 crore aged 1-2 year bucket was not clearly answered.
Recurring bad-debt write-offs (Rs 22-26 crore in H1 and FY26) added back to operating cash flow; the treatment drew analyst challenge and was not fully resolved.
Pricing revision for minimum wages and fuel costs depends on the IBA Working Committee process; timing is uncertain.
Currency supply and ATM dispense per ATM still about 10% below last year; volume recovery depends on pricing clarity.
Related-party loan to an FSS customer: outstanding about Rs 64 crore at September 2026 (including Rs 18 crore disbursed in H1), with Rs 12 crore repaid.
Margin quality: an individual investor argued lease accounting and ESOP costs (about Rs 9 crore in H1) distort EBITDA margin comparisons; management did not quantify the operational share.
Depreciation of about Rs 290-300 crore a year from the FY26 capex and FSS acquisition weighs on PAT.
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline growth, tech and payments mix, and cash flow, and firm on not chasing transaction-linked contracts. Noticeably evasive or unclear on receivable ageing, the cash-flow treatment of bad debts, and the non-ATM volume growth figure, which management deferred to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: And importantly, our second payment segment is now contributing 20% of our services revenue, two quarters ahead of our forecast.
All of our new business wins are on a fixed fee contract basis.
In the first half of this year, our capex in these ATMs were 10.6 crores down 63% from last year and limited to deployments which we were already committed to.
We walked away from a large 700 crores contract which was priced at levels we did not accept.
Acquisitions happen only at the right value as they did with Securance and FSS CashTech.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 EBITDA margin rose 290 bps to 27% and FY27 margin guidance is about 27%; depreciation is set to peak in FY27 and fall as a share of revenue from FY28, with EBITDA growth flowing more to earnings. Minimum-wage and fuel cost pressure and unresolved IBA repricing cap the upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: FY27 capex guided to Rs 100-125 crore versus Rs 351 crore in FY26 and H1 net capex was Rs 50 crore; offsite ATMs fell from about 88,000 to 70,000 and ATM capex is down 63% YoY, so no new capacity is being added.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 order wins were about Rs 700 crore, ATM and retail solutions grew about 10% Q2 on Q2, and dispense per ATM is still about 10% below last year, so recovery has room; pricing talks with IBA are expected to resolve in Q3-Q4.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not disclosed, and management cut capex sharply in the stressed part of the business (Rs 351 crore to Rs 100-125 crore), so a new capex programme is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 services revenue guidance was held at Rs 2,650-2,750 crore and EBITDA margin at about 27%; H1 services revenue is Rs 1,269 crore, so upside depends on H2 product deliveries and pricing.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Services guidance of Rs 2,650-2,750 crore needs H2 services of roughly Rs 1,381-1,481 crore, about 9-17% above H1's Rs 1,269 crore, and pricing revision for minimum wages and fuel depends on the IBA process, which has an uncertain timeline.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Two PSU bank recycler orders won in Q1 are due for delivery in H2 FY27, and an Algo MBS implementation at a new bank goes live in H2 FY27 (rollout across 12,000 machines).

rows.label: IBA revision of cash-management contract prices
rows.why: Minimum wages rose 6% to 60% in key states and fuel costs rose 8%, many contracts were priced years ago, and management is negotiating a revision via the IBA Working Committee with no firm timing.

rows.label: Receivables collection and DSO improvement
rows.why: DSO improved 18-20 days YoY in H1 and management expects collections to be higher in H2, but absolute receivables rose and the Rs 151 crore aged 1-2 year bucket was not clearly reconciled.

rows.label: Surplus cash returned via dividend or buyback
rows.why: Net cash was Rs 373 crore at 30 September after a Rs 168 crore buyback in June and Rs 606 crore returned since listing, with the decision on further returns to be reviewed at fiscal year end.

tone.note: Management was confident on headline growth, Tech & Payments at 20% of services revenue, cash flow and discipline on fixed-fee contracts, but evasive on receivable ageing, the bad-debt cash-flow treatment and the non-ATM volume figure; analysts pressed on receivables, capex accounting, depreciation
